source.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models (METR, Time Horizon 1.1)
source.note: METR times skilled professional software engineers (~5 years' experience) completing real software tasks, using the geometric mean of successful completion times, then reports the task LENGTH (in that human-timed unit) at which frontier models succeed 50%/80% of the time. As of Time Horizon 1.1 (page updated 2026-05-08, benchmark METR-Horizon-v1.1 released 2026-04-07), the highest 80%-reliability horizon among tested models is ~186 minutes (Claude Mythos Preview Early) — verified against METR's own published benchmark data, not estimated. METR does NOT publish a breakdown of their task suite by category matching this table's task-type taxonomy (feature/fix/refactor/...) — the per-task-type minutes below are this project's own calibration against that published human-timed scale, not a METR output. These values are unchanged from AegisFlow's earlier illustrative defaults; the METR anchor (feature=240min sits modestly above the current ~186min frontier-model horizon) is an order-of-magnitude sanity check on them, not a re-derivation from METR data. Treat this as a cited industry anchor, not a precise measurement. Refreshable via `aegisflow baseline --refresh --url <manifest>` (no default source — you must supply one you trust; see docs/RETURN-ON-INTELLIGENCE.md §7.1) and, per project, blended with your own git history when enough pre-tracking commits exist — see src/value/liftBaseline.ts.
